additions.rationale: The Torah opens by stating that wine, when a person is 'zakha' (meritorious), 'נעשה ראש' — literally becomes/is the head. This is an explicit bechina: wine-in-its-holy-dimension = rosh. The text: 'יין יש לו שני בחינות: זכה – נעשה ראש, וכשנעשה ראש שהוא בחינות מחין.' The wine becoming head is not a causal statement ('wine causes a head') but an identity statement in the Kabbalistic sense — the wine IS the rosh, the mochin. This edge would connect יין into the ראש/מחין package.

The text explicitly states: 'שלמות המחין, שהם בחינת: שמן משחת קדש, בחינת: כשמן הטוב על הראש, כיידוע.' The mochin are identified with the holy anointing oil (shemen mishchat kodesh) and with the good oil upon the head from Tehilim 133. Shemen (oil) = mochin is a classic Kabbalistic equivalence here stated explicitly. This would add שמן to the ראש/מחין package.

The Torah cites 'ואיש חכם יכפרנה' (Mishlei 16:14) to explain how mochin enable atonement: the wise man = the one who has mochin. Chokhmah and mochin are used interchangeably throughout the passage. The text at line 5: 'עיקר הסליחה – על-ידי החכמה והמחין הקדושים שמקבל בבחינת: ואיש חכם יכפרנה.' Chokhmah is explicitly stated as a bechina of mochin here.

The Torah's analysis of Kaddish: 'יתגדל — תגי דל. תגי, כתר. ישראל הוא בחינת תגי, כי שרית עם אלקים.' Israel = the tagi (crown-tags on letters) = keter. This is an explicit bechina equation. These concepts belong to the Kaddish-analysis cluster (see also new package proposal below).
additions.note: Keter and Yisrael are not yet in any package for Torah #177; if a new Kaddish package were created this edge would anchor it.

additions.rationale: The Torah states: 'רבא – באר. ומשביע לכל חי רצון.' The word 'raba' in Kaddish = a well (be'er) that satisfies all living beings with ratzon. Be'er = ratzon is the stated bechina. This would connect באר into the מלכות/כבוד/רצון package (as ratzon is already there).
The text parses יתגדל as תגי+דל and states 'תגי, כתר' — the crown-tags (tagi) = keter (crown). This is an explicit bechina equation used to interpret Kaddish.

The Torah states: 'כשרוצה האדם איזה רצון אחר חוץ מרצון השם יתברך, על ידי זה נעשה מלכות אחרים של העכו"ם.' A foreign/other will generates foreign kingship — they are identified as the same bechina. This is the evil mirror of the מלכות/כבוד/רצון package: just as holy ratzon = holy malkhut, so too other-ratzon = malkhut-of-idolaters. These two evil concepts share a nature and would form the evil counterpart package.
additions.note: This is the evil mirror of Package #2. Consider creating a separate evil package for מלכות אחרים and רצון אחר.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: יין — wine, the central vehicle of the teaching (has two aspects: zakha→rosh; lo zakha→lower state). Not recorded as a bechina node for Torah #177.
שמן — holy anointing oil, explicitly equated with mochin ('שמן משחת קדש', 'כשמן הטוב על הראש'). Not recorded.
חכמה — wisdom, cited as the instrument of atonement ('ואיש חכם יכפרנה'); equated with mochin in the text. Not recorded for Torah #177.
כפרת עוונות / סליחה — atonement/forgiveness, the practical outcome of the wine→rosh→mochin chain. Appears as eitza target; not yet a bechina node.
כתר — the crown, parsed from 'תגי' in Kaddish analysis. Not recorded.
תגי — the letter-crown tags, parsed from 'יתגדל'. Equated with keter and ישראל. Not recorded.
ישראל — Israel, equated with tagi because 'sarita im Elohim'. Not recorded.
ת"ק שדי — the name Shaddai (spelled as 400+100=500=ת"ק, plus שדי), from analysis of 'יתקדש'. Not recorded.
באר — a well, equated with 'רבא' and 'משביע לכל חי רצון'. Not recorded.
מלכות אחרים — foreign/evil kingship created by a person's alien desires. Not recorded.
רצון אחר — the alien will/desire opposed to God's will. Not recorded.
עלמא דברא — 'the world He created according to His will' (Kaddish phrase); the condition for 'ויַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ'. Not recorded.
analysis_notes.coverage_note: Torah #177 is recorded in the dataset with only 5 bechina edges — extremely sparse for a Torah of this richness. The source text (though brief — only 14 lines) contains at least 7 additional bechina-eligible equations that are not yet in the dataset. The Kaddish analysis section (lines 13–16) in particular is almost entirely unmapped as bechina edges.
